simple.meaning: רִקְמָה (riqmâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “variegation of color ; specifically, embroidery.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Judges 5:30. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רִקְמָה (H7553) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: רִקְמָה (riqmâh) / H7553 is traced through Judges 5:30, 1 Chronicles 29:2, Psalms 45:15, Ezekiel 16:10 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: ‘Have they not found, have they not divided the plunder?

timeline.evidenceText: ‘Have they not found, have they not divided the plunder?
‘Have they not found, have they not divided the plunder?

Now I have prepared with all my might for the house of my God the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, the bronze for the things of bronze, iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood; also onyx stones, stones to be set, stones for inlaid work, of various colors, all kinds of precious stones, and marble stones in abundance.
With gladness and rejoicing they shall be led.
I clothed you also with embroidered work, and put sealskin sandals on you. I dressed you with fine linen and covered you with silk.

Thus you were decked with gold and silver. Your clothing was of fine linen, silk, and embroidered work. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil. You were exceedingly beautiful, and you prospered to royal estate.
You took your embroidered garments, covered them, and set my oil and my incense before them.
and say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says: “A great eagle with great wings and long feathers, full of feathers, which had various colors, came to Lebanon, and took the top of the cedar.

Then all the princes of the sea will come down from their thrones, and lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. They will clothe themselves with trembling. They will sit on the ground, and will tremble every moment, and be astonished at you.
Your sail was of fine linen with embroidered work from Egypt,
“ ‘ “Syria was your merchant by reason of the multitude of your handiworks. They traded for your wares with emeralds, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies.
These were your traders in choice wares, in wrappings of blue and embroidered work, and in chests of rich clothing, bound with cords and made of cedar, among your merchandise.

definitions.usage: broidered (work), divers colours, (raiment of) needlework (on both sides).
definitions.full: H7553. riqmah רִקְמָה noun feminine variegated stuff (woven or embroidered); — absolute ׳ר Judg 5:30 +; suffix רִקְמָתֵךְ Ezek 16:18 , תָם - 26:16 ; dual רִקְמָתַיִם Judg 5:30 ; plural רְקָמוֺת Psa 45:15 ; — (piece of) variegated stuff , Judg 5:30 (twice in verse), for garments Ezek 16:10 , 13 ; 27:16 , 24 ; Psa 45:15 ; explicitly, ר ׳בִּגְדֵי Ezek 16:18 ; 26:16 ; ׳ר apparently = variegated work 27:7 ; figurative of variegated plumage 17:3 ; of variegated stone 1Chr 29:2 .
